name: UniIR
description: Existing information retrieval (IR) models often assume a homogeneous format, limiting their applicability to diverse user needs, such as searching for images with text descriptions, searching for a news article with a headline image, or finding a similar photo with a query image. To approach such different information-seeking demands, we introduce UniIR, a unified instruction-guided multimodal retriever capable of handling eight distinct retrieval tasks across modalities. UniIR, a single retrieval system jointly trained on ten diverse multimodal-IR datasets, interprets user instructions to execute various retrieval tasks, demonstrating robust performance across existing datasets and zero-shot generalization to new tasks. Our experiments highlight that multi-task training and instruction tuning are keys to UniIR's generalization ability. Additionally, we construct the M-BEIR, a multimodal retrieval benchmark with comprehensive results, to standardize the evaluation of universal multimodal information retrieval.
evaluation_method: Recall@k (Recall@1/5/10) and mAP (mean average precision) across datasets
typical_sota_score: varies by dataset; Recall@1 typically ~30–85% depending on modality and dataset
reputation: Introduced a unified multimodal retrieval suite (UniIR) and M-BEIR that have attracted attention for standardizing multimodal IR evaluation but are not yet as widely adopted as single-modality IR benchmarks.
notes: Evaluation varies widely by dataset and modality; reported scores often depend on dataset-specific splits and retrieval protocol. M-BEIR is newer and heterogeneous in dataset size and difficulty; potential contamination from large pretraining corpora for some models.
